561	## The command and the mise tasks (`cmd/nexus-bench`, `mise.toml`)
562	
563	`internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench` is a `package main` of five files:
564	`main.go` (`deps`, `defaultDeps`, `run`), `flags.go` (flags and parameter
565	resolution), `commands.go` (`up`, `provision`, `down`, `render`), `status.go` and
566	`usage.go` (the help). `main()` only builds a context cancelled by SIGINT and
567	SIGTERM, calls `run(ctx, args, os.Getenv, os.Stdout, os.Stderr, defaultDeps())`
568	and exits with its code. `deps` holds every constructor and library call that
569	reaches a cluster (`newRunner`, `newProber`, `clock`, `newStore`, `newInitial`,
570	`preflight`, `deploy`, `provision`, `destroy`); `defaultDeps` wires
571	`NewExecRunner`, `NewProber`, `NewClock`, `NewFileStore`,
572	`NewKubectlInitialPassword`, `RunPreflight`, `Deploy`, `Provision` and `Destroy`,
573	and the tests wire fakes, so no test needs kubectl or a network.
574	
575	**Tasks.** Six, in `mise.toml`, none reachable from `ci`, `check`, `test` or
576	`test-race` (`mise_tasks_test.go` reads the file and checks it, and checks that
577	`kubectl` is declared on each of them, not in the global `[tools]`, so the CI does
578	not install it; kubectl `1.35`, because `datomir` runs k0s v1.36.x and kubectl is
579	supported within one minor version of the API server, so 1.35 is the oldest
580	accepted; `render` contacts no cluster and declares no kubectl, and the test
581	requires its absence there). Arguments follow `--`: mise appends them to the
582	command line.
583	
584	| Task | Runs | Acts on the cluster |
585	|---|---|---|
586	| `nexus-bench:up` | `go run ./internal/nexusbench/cmd/nexus-bench up` | yes |
587	| `nexus-bench:provision` | `... provision` | yes (REST and `exec`) |
588	| `nexus-bench:down` | `... down` | yes (deletes the namespace) |
589	| `nexus-bench:status` | `... status` | reads only |
590	| `nexus-bench:render` | `... render` | no, contacts nothing |
591	| `nexus-bench:test` | `go test -timeout 60m -count=1 -run Integration ./internal/nexusbench/...` with `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` set by the task's `env` table (portable, no `env` command) | yes; the tests skip when `CI` is set |
592	
593	**Subcommands and flags.** Every subcommand takes the same parameter flags, one
594	per `NEXUS_BENCH_*` variable: `--context`, `--namespace`, `--http-nodeport`,
595	`--docker-nodeport`, `--cpu-request`, `--cpu-limit`, `--memory-request`,
596	`--memory-limit`, `--storage-size`, `--jvm-opts`, `--image`, `--image-tag`,
597	`--upstream-url`, `--anonymous`, `--hosts`, `--timeout`, `--delete-timeout`,
598	`--secrets`, `--descriptor`. `up` and `provision` add `--accept-eula` and
599	`--rest-host`. Each subcommand has its own `flag.FlagSet` (`ContinueOnError`,
600	output discarded: the command prints parse errors itself on stderr and `-h` on
601	stdout). A flag is laid over its variable and the result goes through
602	`FromEnv(Defaults(), ...)` once, so "flag, then `NEXUS_BENCH_*`, then default",
603	the parsing and the rule that `--namespace` moves the upstream URL (unless an
604	upstream is given, by flag or variable) are the library's own. `--accept-eula`
605	becomes `yes` (and `--accept-eula=false` `no`, which beats a variable set to
606	`yes`). `Validate` runs before anything else, `render` included.
607	
608	**Exit codes.** `0` success; `1` failure (invalid parameter, kubectl missing, a
609	step failed, a run cancelled); `2` mistake in the command line (no or unknown
610	subcommand, unknown flag, a value of the wrong type, a missing value, an extra
611	argument), with the help on stderr when the subcommand is missing or unknown.
612	`help`, `-h` and `--help` print on stdout and exit `0`. `go run` (so every
613	`mise run nexus-bench:*`) does not propagate the code: it prints `exit status 2`
614	and exits `1`. Code `2` is only visible when the compiled binary is run directly;
615	the general help says so (`TestHelpSaysGoRunDoesNotKeepExitCodeTwo`).
616	
617	**Interruption.** `main()` cancels the run's context on SIGINT or SIGTERM and
618	then hands the signals back to the default behavior (`context.AfterFunc(ctx,
619	stop)`), so a second Ctrl-C kills a run that is slow to wind down. This is not
620	unit-tested: it lives in `main()`, which the tests do not call.
621	
622	**Output.** The progress of the library steps goes to stdout, then one line
623	`nexus-bench: descriptor written to <path>`. Every failure is one line on stderr:
624	a `BenchError` (also when wrapped by `%w` or joined) prints exactly its
625	`Error()`, and nothing around it or inside it (no wrapper text, no `Err`, no
626	trace); a cancelled run says `cancelled` and that `status` shows where things
627	stand; another error prints its message. No output holds a password
628	(`requireClean` of the tests plants markers in the fakes).
629	
630	**`up`.** Resolve the parameters, then the secrets path
631	(`--secrets`/`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else `DefaultSecretsPath`; with no place for
632	it the run stops before any cluster call and says to set
633	`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`), `newRunner`, `newStore` (the git guard), `Deploy` (which
634	runs `RunPreflight(OpUp)` itself, so the command does not run a second one), then
635	`Provision`, then the descriptor. **The descriptor is written only after a
636	successful `Provision`**, never on a failure at any step, and a descriptor from
637	an earlier run is left as it was. It is built with `BuildDescriptor(p,
638	DeployResult, ProvisionResult)`.
639	
640	**`provision`.** `RunPreflight(OpProvision)`, `Provision`, then the descriptor,
641	built with `DeployResult{NodeIP: <node address of the preflight>}`.
642	
643	**`down`.** `Destroy` (its own `RunPreflight(OpDown)` first). The descriptor is
644	not touched or created.
645	
646	**`status`.** Read-only: `RunPreflight(OpStatus)` (a missing namespace is its
647	`NamespaceMissing` error, exit `1`), one `kubectl get pods -l
648	app.kubernetes.io/name=nexus -o json`, one probe of the REST origin, one read of
649	the descriptor. Four lines, each a finding, exit `0`:
650	
651	    bench: namespace nexus-bench, context datomir
652	    pod: running (nexus-xxx, 1/1 ready, 0 restarts)     | not found | pending ...
653	    rest: ready (http://127.0.0.1:30481)                 | not ready (the cause is not shown)
654	    descriptor: matches (<path>) | not found (<path>) | differs from the current parameters (<path>) + one line per field
655	
656	The comparison covers context, namespace, image, both NodePorts, the upstream URL
657	and the anonymous flag; hosts and versions come from the cluster and are left out.
658	It creates no store, builds no `InitialPassword` and sends no credential.
659	
660	**`render`.** Prints `Render(p)` and nothing else; it builds no dependency (the
661	test runs it with an empty `deps`).
662	
663	**Where the credentials go.** `Provision` is given
664	`RESTBaseURL("127.0.0.1", p)`, whatever hosts `Deploy` reached, so the admin and
665	`bench-pull` passwords stay on the loopback by default. `--rest-host <host>`
666	(a host name, an IPv4 or IPv6 address, brackets and a zone allowed; no port,
667	scheme, path, credentials or space, refused before any cluster call with exit
668	`1`) sends them to that host instead, and unless it is a loopback address or
669	`localhost` the command prints on stderr a warning that the credentials travel in
670	clear text. `status` and the deployment wait probe without credentials.
671	
672	**Non-default bench.** After writing the descriptor, if the parameters differ
673	from `Defaults()` (any field but the two timeouts, the two paths, the EULA
674	consent and an empty host list), stderr gets `warning: descriptor.json now
675	describes a non-default bench; do not commit it`. The file is written all the
676	same, at `--descriptor`/`NEXUS_BENCH_DESCRIPTOR`, else the versioned one. A
677	default bench prints nothing on stderr.
678	
679	## Integration tests and source guards (`bench_integration_test.go`, `guard_test.go`, step 9)
680	
681	**Gates.** Every test of `bench_integration_test.go` starts with
682	`requireBench(t)`: it skips unless `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1` and `CI` is empty, so
683	`mise run test`, `check`, `ci` and the CI never reach the cluster. The mise task
684	`nexus-bench:test` sets the variable (`env` table). The destructive test needs
685	two more things: `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1` and `NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes`
686	(the lifecycle provisions Nexus, so the EULA has to be accepted by the operator).
687	None of the tests writes the versioned `descriptor.json`.
688	
689	**The four tests.** The first three need a bench that is up and provisioned
690	(`mise run nexus-bench:up`): they read the versioned descriptor and the secrets
691	file (`openLiveBench`; the REST URL is the descriptor's one on the loopback) and
692	fail with the command to run when either is missing.
693	
694	| Test | Reads | Writes |
695	|---|---|---|
696	| `TestIntegrationBenchDescribed` | `GET /service/rest/v1/status` without credentials (200), then as admin the repository list and, per repository of the descriptor, its type, format, group members or proxy remote URL | nothing |
697	| `TestIntegrationAnonymousAsDescribed` | the anonymous-access setting as admin, and `GET /repositories` without credentials: 200 when the descriptor says anonymous is enabled, 401 when not | nothing |
698	| `TestIntegrationPullAccountIsReadOnly` | `GET /repositories` as `bench-pull` (200) | one control `POST` of a hosted repository `bench-readonly-probe` as `bench-pull`, which has to be refused with **403**. If Nexus accepts it (any 2xx), the test deletes that repository as admin and fails |
699	| `TestIntegrationLifecycle` | admin listings of repositories, roles and users | destructive, see below |
700	
701	`TestIntegrationLifecycle` runs `Deploy` and `Provision` (first up), compares a
702	snapshot of repositories, roles and users, runs up and provision a second time
703	and requires the same snapshot (idempotence), then `Destroy` and checks that
704	`get namespace` answers NotFound, `Deploy` on a fresh instance (the pod must hold
705	an `admin.password` again), and a final `Destroy`. It uses the parameters of
706	`FromEnv` and the secrets path of the bench (`NEXUS_BENCH_SECRETS`, else the
707	default), refuses to start without the EULA, and refuses when `go test` has less
708	than 45 minutes left (`lifecycleMinTimeout`: three deployments of up to ten
709	minutes plus the deletions; the default of `go test` is 10 minutes). The
710	namespace is whatever the parameters say; the preflight already refuses a
711	namespace this tool did not create.
712	
713	**Running it.** The task passes `-timeout 60m` for that reason
714	(`TestMiseBenchTestTaskRunsTheIntegrationTestsGuarded` requires a `-timeout` of
715	at least 45 minutes):
716	
717	    mise run nexus-bench:test                         # the three read tests, lifecycle skipped
718	    DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_LIFECYCLE=1 NEXUS_BENCH_ACCEPT_EULA=yes mise run nexus-bench:test
719	
720	**A failure leaves the bench deployed.** The lifecycle uses `t.Fatalf` and no
721	cleanup: when a step fails halfway, the namespace stays as it is so that the
722	cause can be diagnosed (`nexus-bench status`, `kubectl logs`). Clean up with
723	`mise run nexus-bench:down`.
724	
725	**Source guards (`guard_test.go`).** Three tests read the package with
726	`go/parser`, name file and line, and each detector has a self-test fed with a
727	faulty and a correct source held in memory. A failure points at code that breaks
728	the rule, not at a test to relax.
729	
730	1. *Every test that reaches the bench calls `requireBench(t)` first.* A call of
731	   `NewExecRunner`, `DescriptorPath`, `DefaultSecretsPath` or `newClient` (unless
732	   `newClient` is given the address of an `httptest` server) before the guard, or
733	   in a function without it, fails. Exceptions are named in
734	   `requireBenchExceptions`, with a `check` that verifies the reason in the
735	   source (the PATH is isolated, the environment is a map); an exception that
736	   matches nothing fails too (`TestGuardExceptionsStillMatch`). Limit: calls are
737	   read by name in the test files of this folder; a call hidden behind a function
738	   value, or made by the tests of `cmd/nexus-bench` (which run on fakes), is not
739	   seen.
740	2. *Only `kubectl.go` and `secrets.go` start a process* (`exec.Command` or
741	   `CommandContext`, any import name, dot import refused): one door to the
742	   cluster, one to `git check-ignore`. A listed file that no longer starts one
743	   must be dropped from the list. Limit: `syscall.Exec`, `os.StartProcess` and a
744	   process started by another package are not seen.
745	3. *No Authorization header outside the client.* The word `authorization` (in an
746	   identifier or a string) may appear only in `nexusapi.go` and `probe.go`,
747	   `SetBasicAuth` only in `nexusapi.go`, and `net/http/httputil` is imported
748	   nowhere. Comments are not read. Limit: a header name built by concatenation,
749	   or a whole `http.Header` printed with `%v`, is not seen.
750

752	line-based reader (no TOML library in `go.mod`) and checks: the six tasks exist
753	and call the command; none of `ci`, `check`, `test`, `test-race` reaches a
754	`nexus-bench` task, directly or through `depends` and `run` references; `kubectl`
755	is declared on `up`, `provision`, `down`, `status` and `test`, absent on `render`

757	`DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH=1`, runs `-run Integration` and carries a `-timeout` of at
758	least 45 minutes. Limit: it reads the file, it does not ask mise to resolve it.
759	
760	## Still to come
761	
762	The first real run on `datomir` (step 10, blocked on the EULA and cluster-access

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |

### Status Monitoring System

**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks

Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.

**Parallel Execution:**
- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`

### Component CRUD Operations

Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`

State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one.

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view.

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`

**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.

**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

could be lowered, but it was kept (the JVM grows with the first pulls, to be
measured with NX-02). `/nexus-data` held 3.7 MB. `admin.password` is gone once

existing, already provisioned namespace takes 1 to 2 s.

200, `POST /repositories/docker/hosted` 201, `POST .../group` 201, `PUT
/security/roles/{id}` 204, `PUT /security/users/{id}` 204, `PUT

.../group/{name}` 204. The swagger lists the same codes (`GET /v1/system/eula`

swagger and the instance do.

input.message:
Phase B is done. One H-REST hypothesis was wrong and is fixed in the client and the fake. Everything else ran green on datomir, and the cluster is back to its pre-bench state. Nothing is committed. No password appears anywhere in this report.

**Step 1, first `up` on the existing instance**
- Read: Nexus 3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY), stored admin password accepted.
- Written: EULA accepted, realms set, anonymous on, role `bench-docker-pull`, user `bench-pull`, `docker-hosted` created.
- Failed: `POST docker/proxy` returned HTTP 400, so `up` exited 1. This was a real divergence from H-REST.
- Cause: Nexus resolves the proxy's remote URL host when it saves the repository. The body is `[{"id":"HelperBean.proxy.remoteUrl","message":"Proxy URL blocked: Failed to resolve host: ..."}]`, content type `application/vnd.siesta-validation-errors-v1+json`.
- I got that body with one more refused POST of the same payload (nothing created, no password printed).
- Fix, tests first (compile-red, then green):
  - `internal/nexusbench/provision_upstream_test.go` (new): five tests plus the descriptor test.
  - `fakenexus_test.go`: `BlockUpstream`, `ResolveUpstream` and the real 400 answer on POST and PUT of a proxy.
  - `nexusapi.go`: `APIError.RemoteURLBlocked`. The body is parsed for that verdict only; no text of it is kept or printed.
  - `provision.go`: on that verdict, the proxy is skipped with `provision: warning: Nexus cannot resolve the upstream host of docker-proxy ...`. The group is created with `docker-hosted` only. `ProvisionResult.ProxyPending` is true only when the proxy does not exist. Any other 400 still fails.
  - `descriptor.go`: with `ProxyPending`, `BuildDescriptor` lists neither the proxy nor the group member.
- This is a design choice of mine: without it `up` can never succeed before NX-02. You can revert it.
- Re-run: exit 0 in 2 s, group created, `descriptor.json` written.
- Your "fake returns 201 on POST users/roles" point was already aligned. The fake already returned 200 for those and 201 for repositories, which matches the swagger, so I changed nothing there.

**Step 2, second `up`**
- Exit 0 in 1 s, no error, no duplicate.
- `descriptor.json` is byte-identical (`cmp`). `git diff --stat` has no baseline because the file is still untracked.
- The client sent no POST except the refused one for the pending proxy, which is a consequence of the fix. It does `PUT` everything else, including `PUT change-password` for `bench-pull` with the same stored password.

**Step 3, read-only integration tests**
- 3 PASS (8 subtests): `BenchDescribed`, `AnonymousAsDescribed`, `PullAccountIsReadOnly`.
- The control POST as `bench-pull` got 403, and nothing was created.

**Step 4, measures**

| Measure | Value |
|---|---|
| Idle load after provisioning | 55m CPU, 1257Mi memory |
| Image | `docker.io/sonatype/nexus3:3.98.1` |
| `/nexus-data` | 3.7 MB |
| `admin.password` | gone after the password change |
| `Server` header | `Nexus/3.98.1-01 (COMMUNITY)` |
| `up` on an empty namespace (phase A) | 48 s |
| `up` on an already provisioned instance | 1 to 2 s |

HTTP statuses seen in Nexus's `request.log`:
- 204: `PUT` admin change-password, `POST` eula, `PUT` realms, `PUT` role, `PUT` user, `PUT` user change-password, `PUT` hosted and group repositories.
- 200: `PUT` anonymous, `POST` roles, `POST` users.
- 201: `POST` hosted and group repositories.
- 400: `POST` proxy, with the cause above.
- 403: the `bench-pull` control POST.

**Step 5, destructive lifecycle**
- `TestIntegrationLifecycle` PASS in 151 s: up, provision, up and provision with no change, down, up on a fresh instance, down.
- `get ns nexus-bench` returns NotFound, no PV of the bench remains, and `secrets.json` is gone.
- `descriptor.json` is unchanged. One leftover: an empty `~/.local/state/devdesk/nexus-bench/datomir/` folder. `Remove` only deletes the namespace folder.

**Step 6, checks**
- `gofmt -l`: clean. `go vet ./...`: clean. `golangci-lint run ./internal/nexusbench/...`: 0 issues.
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/nexusbench/...`: ok (integration tests skipped without the variable).
- `go test -race -count=2 ./internal/nexusbench/...`: ok.

**Step 7, doc**
- `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md` now has a "First real run" section and a "validated on datomir 2026-11-16" status.
- It also records the H-REST verdict, the pending-proxy behaviour, the idempotence caveat and a rewritten "Still to come" (step 10 removed, NX-02 next).
- I did not touch `docs/product/nexus-support/stories.md`.

**Git status**
- Modified: `docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md` and, under `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.worktrees/feat-nexus-bench-504/internal/nexusbench/`, `descriptor.go`, `fakenexus_test.go`, `nexusapi.go`, `provision.go`.
- New: `provision_upstream_test.go`, and `descriptor.json`, the generated descriptor to commit (no proxy, group is `docker-hosted` only).
- Not mine: `.claude/plans/DEVDESK-504-plan.md`.
- Scratch files are in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-anthoni-projects-workspace-entire-anthnel-devdesk/25d7becf-d3c5-436d-8404-57c7cd7a1db0/scratchpad/step10/`, including `descriptor.run1.json`.

**Cluster**
- Namespace `nexus-bench` is deleted and no orphan PV remains. No incident: no OOM, no stuck Terminating. I did not touch anything outside `nexus-bench`.

**Open points**
- NX-02 must deploy `bench-upstream`. Then run `up` again, which creates the proxy and adds it to the group, and recommit the descriptor.
- The committed descriptor shows the pre-NX-02 state. It has no proxy and a one-member group.
- Whether to keep the 3Gi memory request given 1.26 Gi at idle: I kept it, to be measured under pull load with NX-02.
